page: Google Cloud Platform c3-highcpu-176 is a compute-optimized server instance featuring 176 vCPUs mapped to 88 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8481C processor. Operating at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this dedicated CPU allocation includes 105 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512). The system is configured with 352 GB of RAM, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 10% of tested systems. The instance exhibits high memory bandwidth, reaching 458.9 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 190.34 GB/sec for write operations. Cryptographic and vector-heavy operations perform strongly, as evidenced by top-tier scores in PassMark CPU extended instructions and encryption tests. However, single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling in the middle 50% range.

From a resource density perspective, the c3-highcpu-176 offers high compute density per unit of memory, making it a cost-efficient option for parallelized workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The primary tradeoff is the low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core, which may bottleneck memory-bound applications. Additionally, the lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which can impact I/O-heavy operations.

This instance is suited for highly parallelized, compute-intensive workloads. Appropriate applications include multi-threaded software compilation, ray tracing, image processing, static web serving, and medium-scale LLM inference prompt processing. It is also applicable for high-throughput database operations and Redis deployments that fit within the 352 GB memory limit.
